subject: maths
title: Primary 2 3D Shapes: Cube, Cuboid, Cylinder, Cone and Sphere
seo_title: P2 3D Shapes Worksheets: Free Primary 2 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Identifying, naming, describing and classifying 3D shapes: cube, cuboid, cone, cylinder, sphere
meta_desc: Free P2 maths practice: name cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones and spheres, count flat and curved faces, roll, stack or slide. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A cube has 6 square faces of the same size; any other box is a cuboid.
key_sub: A cylinder has 2 flat faces and 1 curved face, so it can roll, stack and slide.

faq.q: What 3D shapes do P2 students learn?
faq.a: Primary 2 students learn to name, describe and sort five 3D shapes: cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone and sphere. They look at flat and curved faces and at which shapes can roll, stack or slide.

faq.q: How do I explain the difference between a cube and a cuboid to my child?
faq.a: A cube has 6 faces that are all squares of the same size, like a die. A cuboid has rectangle faces, like a box of tissues or a shoebox.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with 3D shapes in P2?
faq.a: Children often use 2D names for 3D shapes, such as calling a ball a circle or an ice cream cone a triangle. Let them hold real objects and feel the flat and curved faces.

faq.q: Is this topic in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Identifying, naming, describing and classifying the cube, cuboid, cone, cylinder and sphere is part of Geometry in the MOE 2021 Primary 2 Mathematics syllabus.

items.q: What is the name of this 3D shape?
items.e: It has 6 flat faces. They are all squares of the same size. So it is a cube.

items.q: Name this 3D shape.
items.e: It has 6 flat faces. They are rectangles, not all squares. So it is a cuboid, not a cube.
It has 2 flat faces that are circles and 1 curved face. So it is a cylinder. It has no pointed tip like a cone.
It has 1 flat face that is a circle, a curved face and a pointed tip. So it is a cone.
It is round all over, like a ball. So it is a sphere. A circle is flat; a sphere is solid.

items.q: What is this shape called?
items.e: It has 6 flat faces. They are all squares of the same size. So it is a cube. It is turned, but it is still a cube.

items.q: What is the name of this 3D shape?
items.e: It has 6 flat faces. They are rectangles, not all squares. So it is a cuboid, not a cube. It is standing on its end, but it is still a cuboid.
It has 2 flat faces that are circles and 1 curved face. So it is a cylinder. It has no pointed tip like a cone. It is lying on its side, but it is still a cylinder.
It has 1 flat face that is a circle, a curved face and a pointed tip. So it is a cone. It is upside down, but it is still a cone.

items.q: What is the name of this 3D shape?
items.e: It has 6 flat faces. They are rectangles, not all squares. So it is a cuboid, not a cube. It is turned, but it is still a cuboid.
It has 2 flat faces that are circles and 1 curved face. So it is a cylinder. It has no pointed tip like a cone. It is short, like a coin, but it is still a cylinder.
It has 1 flat face that is a circle, a curved face and a pointed tip. So it is a cone. It is lying on its side, but it is still a cone.
It has 2 flat faces that are circles and 1 curved face. So it is a cylinder. It has no pointed tip like a cone. It is tall and thin, but it is still a cylinder.

items.q: Name this 3D shape.
items.e: It has 6 flat faces. They are rectangles, not all squares. So it is a cuboid, not a cube. The 2 end faces are squares, but the other 4 faces are long rectangles. In a cube, all 6 faces are squares.

items.q: Which of these is a flat 2D shape?
items.e: A circle is flat. You can draw it on paper. A sphere, a cube and a cone are solid 3D shapes.
D is a cuboid. Its flat faces are rectangles. The cube has only square faces, the cylinder has a curved face and the square is a flat 2D shape.
A is a sphere. It is round all over, like a ball. The plain circle is a flat 2D shape, not a sphere.
B is a cone. It has a flat circle face and a pointed tip. The triangle is a flat 2D shape.

items.q: Which picture shows a cube?
items.e: C is a cube. All its faces are squares of the same size. The two long boxes are cuboids. The square is a flat 2D shape.
It has 2 flat faces that are circles and 1 curved face. So it is a cylinder. It has no pointed tip like a cone. Turning a shape does not change its name.
A die has 6 flat faces. They are all squares of the same size. So it is a cube.

items.q: This is a box of tissues. What 3D shape is it?
items.e: A box of tissues has 6 flat faces. They are rectangles, not all squares. So it is a cuboid.
A tin has 2 flat circle faces (top and bottom) and a curved face. So it is a cylinder.
A ball is round all over. So it is a sphere. A circle is flat; a ball is solid.
It has a round opening at the top and a pointed tip at the bottom. So it is a cone. From the side it looks like a triangle, but a triangle is flat.
The scoop is round all over, like a ball. So it is most like a sphere.

items.q: Families give mandarin oranges at Chinese New Year. What 3D shape is a mandarin orange most like?
items.e: A mandarin orange is round all over, so it is most like a sphere. A circle is a flat 2D shape.
It has a round opening at the bottom and a pointed tip at the top. So it is a cone.

items.q: A shoebox is shaped like a …
items.e: A shoebox has 6 flat faces that are rectangles. So it is a cuboid.

items.q: A candle is shaped like a …
items.e: A candle has a flat circle face at each end and a curved face. So it is a cylinder.

items.q: A marble is shaped like a …
items.e: A marble is round all over. So it is a sphere.

items.q: A packet drink is shaped like a …
items.e: A packet drink has 6 flat faces. They are rectangles, not all squares. So it is a cuboid.

items.q: A brick is shaped like a …
items.e: A brick has 6 flat faces. They are rectangles, not all squares. So it is a cuboid.

items.q: A round birthday cake is shaped like a …
items.e: A round cake has a flat circle top, a flat circle bottom and a curved side. So it is a cylinder.

items.q: A toy block with 6 square faces of the same size is shaped like a …
items.e: 6 flat faces that are all the same square: it is a cube, not a cuboid.
B is a tin. It has 2 flat circle faces and a curved face, so it is a cylinder. The die is a cube, the box is a cuboid and the ball is a sphere.
A is a die. All its faces are squares of the same size, so it is a cube. The box of tissues is a cuboid, the tin is a cylinder and the hat is a cone.
C is a mandarin orange. It is round all over, so it is most like a sphere. The tin is a cylinder, the hat is a cone and the box is a cuboid.

items.q: Siti says a ball is a circle. Is she correct?
c: No. A ball is a sphere.
No. A ball is a cylinder.
items.e: A circle is flat. You can draw it on paper. A ball is solid and round all over, so it is a sphere.

items.q: Hafiz says a box of tissues is a cube. Is he correct?
items.e: A cube and a cuboid both have 6 flat faces. In a cube they are all squares of the same size. A box of tissues has long rectangle faces, so it is a cuboid.

items.q: How many flat faces does a cube have?
items.e: A cube has 6 flat faces. In the picture you can see only 3. The other 3 are at the back and at the bottom: 3 + 3 = 6.

items.q: How many flat faces does a cuboid have?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 flat faces: top and bottom, front and back, and 2 ends. You can see only 3 of them.
A cylinder has 2 flat faces: a circle at the top and a circle at the bottom. The curved face is not flat, so do not count it.
A cone has 1 flat face: the circle at the bottom. The rest is a curved face.
A sphere is round all over. It has no flat faces, only a curved face.
A cylinder has 1 curved face that goes all the way round. Its 2 circle faces are flat.
A sphere has 1 curved face that goes all the way round. It has no flat faces.

items.q: What shape is each face of a cube?
items.e: All 6 faces of a cube are squares of the same size. The cube is 3D; each face is a flat square.

items.q: What shape are the faces of this cuboid?
items.e: The faces of this cuboid are rectangles. A cuboid is a 3D shape; its faces are flat 2D shapes.
The flat faces of a cylinder are circles. In a picture they look squashed because we see them from the side.
The flat face of a cone is a circle. From the side a cone looks like a triangle, but it has no triangle face.

items.q: Which shape has only flat faces?
items.e: A cube has 6 flat faces and no curved face. A cylinder and a cone have a curved face too. A sphere has only a curved face.

items.q: Which shape has only a curved face?
items.e: A sphere has 1 curved face and no flat faces. A cylinder and a cone also have flat faces.

items.q: Which shape has 1 flat face and 1 curved face?
items.e: A cone has 1 flat circle face and 1 curved face. A cylinder has 2 flat faces.

items.q: Which shape has 2 flat faces and 1 curved face?
items.e: A cylinder has 2 flat circle faces and 1 curved face. A cone has only 1 flat face.

items.q: Hui Min draws around the bottom of a tin of milk. What shape does she draw?
items.e: The tin is a cylinder. Its bottom face is a flat circle, so Hui Min draws a circle.

items.q: Kumar dips one face of a die in paint and presses it on paper. What shape does he print?
items.e: Every face of a die (a cube) is a square, so the print is a square. A print is flat, so it cannot be a cube.

items.q: Mei Ling counts the flat faces of a cube in a picture and gets 3. What did she forget?
items.e: A picture shows only 3 faces of a cube. There are 3 more at the back and at the bottom. 3 + 3 = 6 flat faces.
D is a cylinder. It has a curved face. The cube and the cuboids have only flat faces.
B is a sphere. It has only a curved face. The cylinder has 2 flat faces, the cone has 1 and the cube has 6.
A sphere has only a curved face. It rolls, but it cannot stack or slide.

items.q: What can this shape do?
items.e: A cube has only flat faces. It can stack and slide on its flat faces. It has no curved face, so it cannot roll.
A cylinder rolls on its curved face. It stacks and slides on its 2 flat faces. So it can do all three.
A cone rolls on its curved face and slides on its flat face. It has a pointed tip, so you cannot stack a shape on it.

items.q: What can this shape do?
items.e: A cuboid has only flat faces. It can stack and slide. It has no curved face, so it cannot roll.

items.q: Which shape can roll and can also be stacked?
items.e: A cylinder rolls on its curved face and stacks on its flat faces. A sphere and a cone roll, but you cannot stack on them. A cube stacks, but it cannot roll.

items.q: Which shape can roll but cannot slide?
items.e: A sphere has no flat face to slide on, so it always rolls. A cylinder and a cone can slide on a flat face.

items.q: Which shape can slide but cannot roll?
items.e: A cuboid has only flat faces, so it slides but cannot roll. The other shapes have a curved face, so they can roll.

items.q: Why can a sphere roll?
items.e: Shapes roll on a curved face. A sphere is curved all over, so it rolls easily.

items.q: Why can you not put a box on top of a cone?
c: The cone has a flat face.
The cone has a pointed tip.
items.e: The top of a cone is a pointed tip, not a flat face. A box on top would fall off.

c: It rolls: it has a curved face.
It slides: it has a flat face.
It rolls: it has flat faces.
It slides: it has a curved face.
items.e: The cylinder is lying on its curved face, so it rolls down the slope.

c: It rolls: it has flat faces.
It slides: it has a curved face.
It slides: it has a flat face.
It rolls: it has a curved face.
items.e: The cylinder is standing on a flat circle face. A flat face does not roll, so it slides down.

items.q: Mr Tan puts this cube on a slope, on one of its flat faces. It moves down the slope. What does it do?
c: It slides: it has a flat face.
It slides: it has a curved face.
It rolls: it has a curved face.
It rolls: it has flat faces.
items.e: A cube has only flat faces, so it cannot roll. It slides down the slope.

c: It slides: it has a flat face.
It slides: it has a curved face.
It rolls: it has flat faces.
It rolls: it has a curved face.
items.e: A sphere has only a curved face, so it rolls down the slope.

items.q: Jun Jie builds a tower of shapes. Which shape can only go at the very top?
items.e: A cone has a flat face at the bottom, so it can sit on the tower. Its pointed tip means nothing can go on it. Cubes, cuboids and cylinders can go anywhere in the tower.

items.q: A cone lies on its curved face. You push it. How does it roll?
items.e: A cone rolls round and round its pointed tip, so it moves in a circle. A cylinder rolls in a straight line.

items.q: Which shape can roll in every direction?
items.e: A sphere is curved all over, so it can roll any way. A cylinder rolls only forwards or backwards. A cone rolls in a circle. A cube cannot roll.
C is a cylinder. It rolls on its curved face. The cube and the cuboids have only flat faces, so they cannot roll.
B is a cuboid. It has only flat faces, so it cannot roll. The cylinder, the cone and the sphere all have a curved face, so they can roll.

items.q: Nurul says a cylinder cannot roll because it has flat faces. Is she correct?
c: Yes. Only a sphere can roll.
No. It rolls on its flat faces.
No. It rolls on its curved face.
items.e: A cylinder has 2 flat faces and 1 curved face. Lying on its curved face, it rolls. Standing on a flat face, it can stack or slide.
The shapes with a curved face can roll: 2 cylinders, 1 sphere and 1 cone. 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. Do not forget the cone.
There are 3 cuboids. The long shape with square ends is a cuboid too: its other 4 faces are long rectangles. The 2 cubes are not cuboids: all their faces are squares of the same size.
Only the cube and the cuboid have no curved face: 2 shapes. The cylinders and the cone have flat faces, but they have a curved face too.
The bottom part has 2 flat circle faces and a curved face: a cylinder. The top has a pointed tip: a cone. A triangle is flat.

items.q:
Devi sorts shapes into two groups.
Group A: cube, cuboid
Group B: cylinder, cone, sphere
What is the rule for Group B?
items.e: A cylinder, a cone and a sphere all have a curved face, so they can roll. The cube and the cuboid cannot roll.

items.q:
Ethan sorts shapes into two groups.
Group A: cube, cuboid, cylinder
Group B: cone, sphere
What is the rule for Group A?
items.e: A cube, a cuboid and a cylinder have flat faces at the top and bottom, so they can be stacked. A cylinder has a curved face, so “only flat faces” is not the rule.
C is a cone. It has a pointed tip, so you cannot stack a shape on it. The cube, the cylinder and the cuboid have flat faces at the top and bottom.

items.q: I have 6 flat faces. They are all squares. What am I?
items.e: 6 flat faces that are all squares of the same size: a cube.

items.q: I can roll. I have 2 flat faces. What am I?
items.e: A cylinder rolls on its curved face and has 2 flat circle faces. A cone has only 1 flat face.

items.q: I have only a curved face. I cannot be stacked. What am I?
items.e: A sphere has 1 curved face and no flat faces. A circle is flat, not a 3D shape.

items.q: I have 1 flat face and a pointed tip. What am I?
items.e: A cone has 1 flat circle face and a pointed tip. A triangle is a flat 2D shape.

items.q: Xin Yi has 2 tins of milk. How many flat faces do the 2 tins have altogether?
items.e: Each tin is a cylinder with 2 flat faces. 2 + 2 = 4. (6 also counts the curved faces, which are not flat.)

items.q: Ahmad has 4 party hats shaped like cones. He draws around the flat face of each hat. How many circles does he draw?
items.e: A cone has 1 flat face, a circle. 4 hats give 4 circles. (8 gives each cone 2 flat faces, like a cylinder.)

items.q: Zhi Hao has 3 dice. He counts all the faces of the 3 dice. How many faces are there?
items.e: Each die is a cube with 6 faces. 6 + 6 + 6 = 18. (9 counts only the 3 faces you can see on each die.)

items.q: Farah has 1 cube, 2 cuboids, 3 cylinders, 2 spheres and 1 cone. She puts all the shapes that can roll in a box. How many shapes are in the box?
items.e: Cylinders, spheres and cones can roll. 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. Do not forget the cone.

items.q: Mrs Lim has 46 cubes and 28 cylinders. How many more cubes than cylinders does she have?
items.e: Find the difference: 46 − 28 = 18. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 16 − 8 = 8, 3 − 2 = 1. (22 comes from 8 − 6 instead of renaming.)

items.q: Wei Ming uses 35 cuboids and 27 cones to build a model. How many shapes does he use altogether?
items.e: Add the parts: 35 + 27 = 62. 5 + 7 = 12 ones: rename 10 ones as 1 ten. (52 forgets the new ten; 512 writes 12 next to 5.)

items.q: A shop packs 5 balls in each box. How many balls are there in 4 boxes?
items.e: 1 unit = 5 balls. 4 units = 4 × 5 = 20 balls. (9 adds 4 + 5 instead.)

items.q: Kavya has 24 marbles. She puts them equally into 3 bags. How many marbles are in each bag?
items.e: 3 units = 24. 1 unit = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 marbles. (21 takes away 3 instead of dividing.)

items.q: There are 50 shapes in a box. 18 are cones. The rest are cylinders. How many cylinders are there?
items.e: Whole − part: 50 − 18 = 32. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 10 − 8 = 2, 4 − 1 = 3. (48 comes from 8 − 0; 68 adds instead of subtracting.)
